meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal common law system; Quebec private law follows the civil law tradition)

Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Parts XII.2 and II.1; Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Status (Good Standing) of any foreign corporate shareholder or corporate UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada became Party to the Hague Apostille Convention effective 11 January 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address for each non-resident director and each Individual with Significant Control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority / national ID issuer / bank reference of the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles / Charter, constitutional documents, and director/shareholder register of any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry / notary public of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English or French translation of all non-English / non-French documents, with translator's notarized declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization only; no apostille required for the translation declaration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening against: (i) the consolidated Canadian sanctions list administered by Global Affairs Canada under SEMA and the United Nations Act; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, given the designated USD payment rails (Stripe/PayPal); (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) domestic/foreign PEP and Head of International Organizations (HIO) databases per FINTRAC obligations and FATF Recommendation 12; and (v) adverse media / negative news. Automated dropshipping is classified Medium_Risk_Enhanced, requiring enhanced due diligence on major suppliers, verification of payment-processing account beneficial owners, and annual re-screening of all directors and UBOs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) - https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/cd-dgc.nsf/eng/home
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English, French, or a bilingual format and must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element (Corporation, Incorporated, Inc., Corp., Ltd., or Limitee). A mandatory NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report dated within 90 days preceding filing must accompany the Articles of Incorporation to confirm distinguishability from existing Canadian corporate names and registered trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, Corporations Canada provides written reasons on request pursuant to CBCA s. 12(2). The applicant may file a written reconsideration request with a proposed corrected name within 30 days of receipt of reasons; no statutory reconsideration fee applies. If the Director maintains the refusal, the applicant must obtain a fresh NUANS report and file amended articles under a revised name, or seek judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada within 30 days of the final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable subject to CBCA s. 19: the registered office must be a physical street address within the province or territory named in the articles, accessible during normal business hours for service of process. P.O. box addresses are prohibited. Virtual office and registered-agent mail-forwarding arrangements satisfy the statutory requirement in practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; approximately 10-15% probability of a physical verification visit within the first 3 years, driven by CRA GST/HST registration onboarding, FINTRAC compliance examinations, and enhanced due diligence field checks triggered by the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification of automated dropshipping merchants.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal government fee for online filing of Articles of Incorporation (single-class shares)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff: CAD 200 for online filing (CAD 250 by paper)
Statutory core fee CAD 13.80 plus prevailing market service-provider markup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal preparation of Articles, by-laws, minute book, and director/UBO questionnaires
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard CBCA single-class share incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and corporate records/agent service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: CAD 200 - CAD 400 per year for a physical registered office in Ontario or Quebec

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, translation, and Hague Apostille bundle for non-resident directors and corporate UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, certified translator, and authentication service (Global Affairs Canada or authorized apostille agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fees; Global Affairs Canada authentication fee approximately CAD 30 per document plus notary and translation fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT PEP, sanctions, and adverse media screening of directors and UBOs (pre-incorporation report)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial compliance screening provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for an enhanced due diligence screening package for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced entity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended, particularly sections 5 (Incorporation), 8 (Articles of Incorporation), 16 (Registered Office), 106 (First Directors), and 109 (Appointment of Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), Industry Canada Building, 235 Queen Street, Ottawa, ON K1A 0H5
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation (filed online via Corporations Canada’s Online Filing Centre)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the CBCA; shares may be issued without any paid-up amount. No escrow account is required for general non-regulated businesses.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Articles of Incorporation of the corporation be and are hereby adopted. The initial share subscription of 100 common shares is accepted and issued to the founding subscriber at par value. The registered office of the corporation is established at [Registered Office Address], in the Province of Ontario, Canada. The following individuals are hereby appointed as the first directors of the corporation: [Director 1] and [Director 2]. The directors are authorized to open bank accounts, designate signing officers, and transact all ordinary corporate business. Officers shall be appointed at the discretion of the board. This resolution takes effect immediately upon filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada through the NUANS online search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) pre-screen to ensure the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing names, trademarks, and business names. Submit the name reservation request to Corporations Canada or include the name in the online incorporation filing. Alternatively, proceed as a numbered company to bypass name approval.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request (paper or online)
Proposed corporate name and context statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a corrected name request or adopt a numbered company designation by reinstating with new Articles of Amendment before incorporation; no fee penalty is incurred if corrected within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation online, specifying the corporate name, registered office jurisdiction, share structure and restrictions, number of directors, and any special provisions. Verify all data, pay the official filing fee by credit card or online banking, and submit electronically. Upon approval, receive the Certificate of Incorporation in electronic format.
required_dossiers: NUANS name reservation report (if named corporation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by Corporations Canada, files will be adjusted online within 30 days of the notice; any deficiencies in share provisions or director count must be cured by filing amended Articles or providing an explanation to ISED; no re-filing fee if Treasury Board direction applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Initial Registered Office and First Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 3 – Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors. The form must state the exact municipal address of the registered office (not a post office box), postal code, and the names and addresses of each first director. Ensure that each director consents to act in writing. This step adopts the registered office and board composition as resolved by the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Form 3 – Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors
Notice of the registered office address and director contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected due to incomplete director consents or an incorrect registered office address, resubmit the corrected Form 3 online; Corporations Canada will process the correction within 5 business days and may impose a late filing fee only if the statutory 12-month deadline has passed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number Registration and Tax Accounts with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO) portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register for a Corporation Income Tax Account (RT), GST/HST Account (RT) if annual gross revenue exceeds $30,000 or voluntary registration is desired, and Payroll Deductions Account (RP) if employees are hired. Registrations are consolidated under a single Business Number (BN). Submit Form RC1 – Request for a Business Number. Keep corporate banking and CRA correspondence records accurate for future tax filings.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 – Request for a Business Number
Directors’ names, residential addresses, and SINs for registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries information, the taxpayer can respond via My Business Account with supporting documentation; incorrect GST/HST effective dates can be corrected within 30 days without penalty using the GST/HST electronic remittance amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Extra-Provincial Registration and Municipal Licensing Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Companies Office (e.g., Ontario’s Companies and Personal Property Security Branch) and applicable municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the federal corporation carries on business in a province other than the registered office province, file an extra-provincial registration in that province. Verify whether any municipal business license (e.g., online retail, warehousing, home-based business) is required. For pure dropshipping without a physical establishment, consult the municipality where the registered office is located; complete any required municipal license application to maintain compliance with local zoning and taxation by-laws.
required_dossiers: Municipal business license application and fee (if required)
Lease or ownership proof of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a municipality denies a business license, appeal through the local municipal licensing board or adjust the business address; if provincial registration is objected to, pay the prescribed late fee to remedy default and file amended information with the provincial registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping is a remote retail activity with no manufacturing or physical production facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory operating or manufacturing permit is required for dropshipping activities under federal, provincial, or municipal law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) – Not applicable for virtual retail operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – zero physical footprint, no discharge points, no stationary combustion source, and no waste generation from the automated dropshipping business model.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater effluent, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), or regulated hazardous waste are produced by an online intermediation platform that stores no inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – no physical workplace is established; if an administrative office is later used, standard municipal fire code certification, structural load inspection, and occupational health clearance from the provincial occupational health and safety authority (e.g., WSIB in Ontario) will be required under the applicable building code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Registration and filing portal: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/business.html; corporate account administration through CRA My Business Account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine residency: a corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act is Canadian-resident and must file T2 returns. 2. Apply for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) through BRO, selecting program accounts: Corporate Income Tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), Payroll (RP) if employees, and Import/Export (RM) with CBSA if goods cross the border. 3. Register for GST/HST once taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold in a single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive quarters; voluntary registration is available to recover input tax credits. 4. For physical goods exports, activate a CBSA Export Account and file export declarations (Form B13A/e-manifest) via the Canadian Export Reporting System. 5. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must register through BRO or use Form RC8 to obtain a BN and file a T2; a treaty-based waiver of filing is available under s. 150(2.1) ITA. 6. Maintain CRA My Business Account credentials and appoint a Canadian resident representative where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer subject to Part I tax on worldwide income; no pass-through election (e.g., US check-the-box or S-corporation) exists. A corporation controlled by non-residents is a non-CCPC and is denied the small business deduction; income tax is levied at the federal general corporate rate (15% federal plus provincial rates) and Part IV tax applies to certain dividend receipts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box mechanism. Available elections include: (i) subsections 216(1)/217 ITA elections permitting a non-resident to file returns on net Canadian rental or employment income instead of Part XIII withholding; (ii) subsection 273 ETA joint venture election designating one GST/HST registrant to account for tax on the venture's supplies; (iii) Quick Method of Accounting election for GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies not exceeding CAD 400,000; (iv) election to treat a dropshipper and its non-resident customer as having made separate supplies under section 179 ETA; and (v) fiscal-year and instalment-basis elections under subsection 249.1 ITA. Hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 18.4-18.6 ITA) apply mechanistically without elective reclassification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered by CRA under the Excise Tax Act; Quebec administers its own QST but federal GST remains applicable. Provincial retail sales taxes (PST) apply separately in BC, SK, MB, and QC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters ('small supplier' threshold). Non-resident distribution platform operators supplying goods to Canadian consumers through an electronic marketplace are deemed suppliers and must register once the same CAD 30,000 threshold is met in respect of Canadian-market sales; marketplace/digital-service rules effective July 1, 2021.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API tax stamping, or digital invoice clearance mandate exists in Canada. GST/HST returns are filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE (mandatory for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5M). Tax invoices must meet the s. 221/223 ETA requirements (supplier BN, date, description, tax amounts); e-invoicing using XML/EDI is voluntary. CRA requires 6-year retention of sales, purchase, and e-commerce platform records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a supply of goods that are exported by the supplier under the contract of sale is zero-rated under Part V, Schedule VI, ETA, provided credible export evidence exists before the return claiming the zero-rating is filed or within a CRA-accepted extension period. Services: a supply of services to a non-resident is zero-rated under s. 7, Part V, Schedule VI unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or is performed wholly in Canada for a Canadian-resident person; automated dropshipping support services (platform, payment, logistics arrangement) are generally zero-rated when supplied to non-residents not registered for GST/HST. The section 179 ETA drop-shipment rules operate to make both the domestic transfer of goods to a registered non-resident customer and the dropshipper's markup zero-rated where goods are forwarded directly from a Canadian supplier to the foreign end-customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (Form B13A or e-manifest B13C) filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill issued by the common carrier, evidencing physical movement to a foreign destination
Commercial Invoice with exporter/importer legal names, HS classification, quantity, and contract value
Inward Remittance Certificate or payment gateway settlement statement (Stripe/PayPal) evidencing receipt of foreign-currency proceeds
Supporting carrier logs, freight-forwarder certificates, and warehouse outbound manifests demonstrating the goods left Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a zero-rated export as taxable where documentation is deficient, clawing back input tax credits with interest. Penalties: ETA s. 280(1) - 25% of the tax on knowingly false statements; ETA s. 281 - amounts up to 100% of evaded tax for culpable conduct; ETA s. 285 - failures to collect or remit, minimum CAD 250; ITA s. 163(2) - 50% gross-negligence penalty on understated income; criminal liability under ETA s. 327 (up to five years imprisonment and fines), and under the same provision for documentary forgery. CRA's International and Large Business Directorate may also impose director liability under ETA s. 323 for unremitted GST/HST. No statutory Canadian FX-repatriation deadline exists; CRA administratively examines prolonged foreign-currency retention as evidence of domestic consumption, and the 180-day benchmark governs audit due diligence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible foreign exchange regime for both current and capital accounts. Corporate profit remittances are unrestricted subject to tax compliance and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion timeline applies to export receipts. Repatriation occurs freely; however, all FX transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 require mandatory reporting to FINTRAC.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border electronic money issuance by fintech entities is subject to stringent licensing under Canada's Payment Services Act. Offshore EMIs require integration with regulated Canadian banking rails and full compliance with FINTRAC anti-money laundering standards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video verification are permitted for corporate onboarding. In-person interviews are mandated only for high-risk accounts or when regulatory triggers necessitate enhanced due diligence, such as transaction thresholds above CAD 100,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners residing in high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified beneficial ownership declaration, corporate minute book extracts, and source of wealth affidavits
Detailed transaction narrative, independent audit reports, and legal opinions confirming compliance
Bank confirmation letters, equity contribution agreements, and third-party valuation reports

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 100. Required verifications include board resolutions, funding source documentation, and beneficial ownership identification. All such transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 are automatically reported to FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 or MT202 messaging. Commercial Letters of Credit are facilitated through correspondent banks. Purpose codes 200 and 210 apply, supported by commercial invoices, bills of lading, and packing lists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or, after the first return, within 60 days after the anniversary of the last annual return; one return is required per calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing tariff (approx. CAD 50) is imposed after the 60-day period; continuing default for two annual filing cycles permits the Director to issue a notice of default and administratively dissolve the corporation under CBCA s.212; revival requires formal application and additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth calendar month after the corporation's fiscal year-end; a December 31 year-end is due no later than June 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months, or 10% plus 2% per month for repeat failure; interest compounds daily at prescribed rates; repeated non-filing can trigger CRA enforcement, director liability for certain remittances, and administrative dissolution for chronic non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM), annual financial statements and corporate records assembly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; financial statements and executed minutes are retained at the corporation's registered records office and made available to shareholders; when an audit is required, audited statements are signed by the auditor.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 18 months of incorporation and thereafter at least once each calendar year and no later than 15 months after the previous AGM; annual financial statements must be placed before shareholders no later than six months after fiscal year-end unless a valid shareholder waiver applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to call the AGM permits a shareholder to apply to the CBCA Director or a court to order a meeting; late or missing financial statements expose directors to CBCA compliance claims and may support CBCA s.212 dissolution if combined with other persistent defaults.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and audit of statutory registers, including the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with Corporations Canada; register books are retained at the registered office and must be produced to the CBCA Director or law enforcement on lawful demand, and to shareholders under statutory access provisions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Conducted when preparing the annual return and in any event within 60 days after the anniversary date; individual entries must be updated within 15 days after any share transfer or change in significant control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient or absent ISC register is an offence under CBCA Part XXI and may lead to fines on the corporation and/or directors; material misstatements in the register may also be cited in CBCA s.212 dissolution proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No numeric revenue or asset threshold exists under the CBCA. A mandatory independent audit applies to every distributing (public-issuing) federal corporation regardless of size. A non-distributing private CBCA corporation must appoint an auditor each year unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, pass an annual unanimous consent resolution dispensing with the audit under CBCA s.163. Lenders, franchisors or provincial regulators may nevertheless require a full audit or an enhanced review engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public federal corporations must apply International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Private federal corporations may consistently apply Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) or IFRS. Annual financial statements must include the applicable balance sheet, income statement, statement of retained earnings or equity changes, and cash flow statement, and be placed before shareholders at the AGM.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under CBCA s.21.1, each non-reporting federal corporation must take reasonable steps at least once per year to identify every individual with significant control (ISC), defined generally as 25% or more of voting shares or a controlling influence. The register must be updated within 15 days after any share transfer, redemption, option exercise, or change in control. No ISC ledger is filed with Corporations Canada at the federal level; it is maintained on site and is available on lawful demand to the Director, regulatory authorities and, under CBCA access rules, to shareholders. The annual confirmation must reconcile the shareholder ledger to the ISC register and document the date of the review in the minute book.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Register of Debentures (when debentures are outstanding)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–850 per year for registered office/agent services in Canada, including annual return processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–35,000 for a small-to-medium private federal corporation; USD 2,500–8,000 for an annual review engagement when the audit waiver is used

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate (38% base rate less 10% provincial abatement less 13% General Rate Reduction); combined federal-provincial headline rates range from 23% to 31% depending on the province of permanent establishment (the federal jurisdiction alone is 15%, excluding provincial income tax).
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD): 9% federal rate on the first CA$500,000 of active business income, available only to Canadian-controlled private corporations; SBD is fully unavailable to a corporation controlled by non-residents (foreign shareholding disqualifies CCPC status). General Rate Reduction (GRR) applies to non-SBD income. Investment Tax Credits: SR&ED refundable ITC of 35% (CCPC up to CA$3M expenditure limit, otherwise 15%). No statutory tax holiday exists for dropshipping; standard deductions apply (COGS, platform/transaction fees, marketing, CCA) to effective rates substantially below headline once losses and credits are absorbed.
